page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, utilizing two threads per core. Memory capacity is set to 15.0 GB of RAM, equating to 3.75 GB per vCPU. The underlying processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), VAES, and SHA-NI. This server type includes no hardware GPU accelerators and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk needs. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results show balanced single-threaded capabilities offset by limited aggregate throughput. The machine scored 1916.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1835.69 in stress-ng single-core tests, both within average bands. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 14.04 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing achieved 2464.0 points, ranking in the top tier. Conversely, multi-threaded operations reflect the modest 4-vCPU footprint, posting bottom-quartile metrics across stress-ng multi-core (3746.88), Geekbench multi-core (4292.0), Clang compilation (4870.0), and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (27.71 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth recorded 29.4 GB/sec for uncached reads and 18.6 GB/sec for writes, which contributed to lower relative scores in PassMark memory (1626.11) and database operations (2321.04).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-4 provides dedicated Intel Emerald Rapids compute execution with advanced vector instruction support on a small-scale resource footprint. Workloads that rely on instruction acceleration such as AVX-512 and AMX benefit without requiring larger VM instances. However, the absence of local storage and low aggregate multi-core and memory bandwidth present architectural tradeoffs for throughput-heavy tasks.

Appropriate deployments for the c4-standard-4 include general-purpose web serving, lightweight application backends, API endpoints, microservices, and single-threaded data transformation jobs. Workloads demanding high multi-threaded compilation speed, extensive in-memory caching like large-scale Redis clusters, or high-throughput transactional databases will be constrained by the core count and memory bandwidth limits.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor at 2.3 GHz and 15.0 GB of RAM. Running on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and cryptographic acceleration. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the server exhibits solid single-threaded performance, with strong results in bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing, but falls into lower percentiles for multi-core scaling, software compilation, and uncached memory bandwidth. Web serving throughput and small-model LLM prompt processing remain in the mid-range. The c4-standard-4 is best suited for general-purpose workloads, standard web serving, microservices, and lightweight application tiers that benefit from modern Intel instruction sets but do not require heavy parallelization or local disk storage.
